author: h. w. champion
title: Josh Gottheimer highlights student achievements, NYC bus fines controversy, and Flag Day celebration
text:
Rep. Josh Gottheimer, U.S. Congressman representing New Jersey’s 5th district since 2017, shared a series of posts on June 17, 2026, highlighting local achievements and legislative efforts.
In his first post at 13:00 UTC, Gottheimer praised students nominated for military academies: “Every year, our military academy nominees blow me away — in academics, athletics, and community service. These thirty-five students are still so young, yet they’ve already shown an incredible commitment to serving our great country. They represent the very best of our https://t.co/WOCCjSSGUT” .
Later that day at 16:00 UTC, Gottheimer addressed concerns over fines imposed by New York City for idling buses: “NYC pays bottom-feeding bounty hunters to film idling buses and pockets the fines. Some have made more than half a million dollars doing it. Seniors, passengers with disabilities, and children are the ones paying the price. My bipartisan BUSES Act protects passengers and ends https://t.co/aRPiSk45gm” .
At 19:00 UTC, he marked Flag Day celebrations with Bergenfield Mayor Arvin Amatorio and the Benevolent and Protective Order of Elks at Cooper’s Pond Park: “Proud to celebrate Flag Day with Bergenfield Mayor Arvin Amatorio and the Benevolent and Protective Order of Elks at Cooper’s Pond Park. It was a wonderful afternoon honoring our flag and everything it stands for.” .
Gottheimer, who has represented New Jersey’s 5th District since succeeding Scott Garrett in 2017, was born in Livingston in 1975 and resides in Wyckoff. He holds degrees from the University of Pennsylvania (BA) and Harvard University (JD).
